semantics.note: The drafter follows the source closely and keeps 'theoretically'. 'Perfect tool' is rhetorical. The testable core is scaled instruction-directed generation and tweaking output to seem more human.

contract.note: An algorithm 'tuned to evaluate content as human' is in effect a detector, so reading 'seem more human' as evading a classifier is ordinary. Using 2023 as the window and not requiring that every detector be beaten are fair choices.

evidence.note: 52K instruction-following examples generated cheaply with text-davinci-003 in 2023 shows repeatable instruction-directed generation at scale. It is an indirect fit for content aimed at algorithms.
A NeurIPS 2023 controlled study found paraphrasing sharply cut several detectors' accuracy while preserving meaning.
A retrieval defense from the same paper limits any claim that evasion always works. The claim makes no such strong assertion.

reviews.rationale: 2023 evidence shows instruction-directed generation at scale (Alpaca) and controlled tests in which modifying generated text materially lowers detection while keeping meaning (DIPPER). The retrieval defense is context only. 'Perfect' is rhetorical and not scored.

semantics.note: 'Platform algorithms' and 'including generative AI' are inferred from context but fit the surrounding argument. The claim is a present-tense observation of a trend.

contract.note: Readings of practical manipulability using available tools, and of less effort to produce and publish, are ordinary and do not require every algorithm to be vulnerable. The window is evaluator-chosen but reasonable.

evidence.note: Late 2023 reporting: AI-cloned articles first drove a large traffic gain, by Ahrefs estimates. Traffic later fell after Google acted, so the trick was real but not lasting.
January 2024 WIRED reporting: generative AI has 'supercharged' spam summaries, which are now common in Amazon searches. It shows less effort and wider reach but no success rate.
Google's March 2024 disclosure names scaled content abuse as a growing practice and sets out enforcement. It does not measure how well enforcement works.

reviews.rationale: In the window, contemporaneous cases show accessible AI tools producing manipulative content at scale and gaining distribution on Google and Amazon, with less production effort. Google's later reversal and new policies show the success was not permanent. The contract requires neither permanence nor a platform-wide success rate.

evidence.note: Pew, Aug 2026: about 10% of sampled pages show signs of AI authorship. That measures authorship, not whether pages were written for robots, so the antecedent is not established.
Sept 2026 preprint: AI-labeled tokens survive FineWeb filtering. It describes this text as written for human readers, so it does not trace robot-targeted content into models.

reviews.rationale: This is an undated conditional forecast and the antecedent is unknown. No evidence shows that robot-targeted content has become a large chunk of the web, or traces it into later production models. AI-authorship measures are not the same thing. With no conclusive event, the forecast is not scored.
